Journalist Laura Bates on her book Everyday Sexism

Journalist Laura Bates on her book Everyday Sexism Close
Laura Bates is a journalist and the founder of the Everyday Sexism Project, a collection of more than 10,000 women's daily experiences of gender inequality.
She started the project in 2012 and by December 2013 the site had 50,000 entries, including thousands from girls under the age of 18.
Laura told BBC Breakfast why she has now written a book about the issue of routine sexism.

Laura Bates on the #MeToo backlash: 'The idea that men are the victims now is nonsense'

Founder of the Everyday Sexism Project Laura Bates joins BetterPod to discuss the need for institutional reform, #MeToo pushback and her new book, Fix the System, Not the Women.
by: Eliza Pitkin
6 Jul 2022
A still image of Laura Bates speaking at a Ted Talk
Founder of the Everyday Sexism Project, Laura Bates
Share      
Laura Bates is on a mission to pull apart the sexist establishments that shape our society, from schools, media and politics to the criminal justice system.
The 35-year-old writer founded the Everyday Sexism Project in 2012. It’s an ever-growing online platform for people to share their personal encounters with misogyny .
It didn’t take long for Bates to compile the all-too-familiar rhetoric that women and girls hear from childhood, as she quotes: “‘Are you overreacting?’, ‘he didn’t mean it like that’. ‘It’s just boys being boys .’ ‘He probably likes you, take it as a compliment.’ ‘Why didn’t you leave?’. ‘Were you leading him on?’. ‘Have you been drinking?’. ‘What were you wearing?’.
